Rasim Bayramov is a designer and artist exploring collectivity and participation through themes of playfulness, anticipation, bureaucratic structures, and post-colonial reality. These ideas find themselves in websites, installations, printed matter, videos, performances and sculptures.
Rasim has taught classes in Virginia Commonwealth University School of Arts and Middle East Technical University, and has led workshops/talks in Rhode Island School of Design, School for Poetic Computation, VCUarts.
Clients include
For Freedoms, ICA Richmond, Kunsthall Stavanger, David Zwirner Books, Doktar, Turkish Airlines, Refresh, The Anderson, Garanti BBVA, VakıfBank, University of Virginia, School for Poetic Computation, VCUarts, VCUarts Qatar, VCU Douglass Wilder School.

Chameleon

Publication, Print, Poster2025

Chameleon is a publication produced by the VCU Graphic Design MFA students in their second year. Each year a color is chosen and each student writes using that color as a guide. In 2025, the color was Orange 021U. This year's publication was printed on newsprint, 18 x 24 inches.

Memory of Sight

Website, WindowsOS, Mouse, Keyboard, Document camera, Zoom2025
Watch the full Performance here.

Invited by SFPC for a Fall 2025 class, OOPS! , I performed through Zoom simultaneously recorded by a document camera and a web camera. I utilized a writing tool that I developed for an earlier project called "as we speak", where synth and letters on the screen try their best to replace speech.

Kunsthall Stavanger: MC Toolkit

Website, Identity2025
Visit the website here.

Mobilizing Citizenship (MC) was an educational and research project held at Kunsthall Stavanger between 2018 and 2024, which invited both Norwegian and international artists as well as designers to collaborate with young people aged 12 to 16. This toolkit captures the knowledge, experiences, and reflections developed over the course of the project.

Website designed and coded by me and khai tsng
Art direction by nicole killian
Editors: Kristina Ketola Bore and Lee Heinemann

Oxumağı sevmək

Print, Publication, Series2024

“Love to learn” was born from the necessity to examine what and how encyclopedic materials are being presented to a younger population. Transitory nature of editions, volumes and anthologies shape the way important information is being passed down in an easily malleable post-soviet knowledge pool. The publication delves into research on the origins, adaptation and decisions on content, all whilst presenting itself as a children’s encyclopedia in 3 different languages. How can storytelling (or infodumping) through multiple volumes become an un-verbose practice?

2024 VCUArts MFA Thesis Exhibition Identity

Identity, Print, Website2024
Go to the microsite

Deriving from the flowers and plants native to Richmond, I documented their weekly blossoming and layered them with hardworking digital ants made in Blender. Additionally, I also developed a micro-site using p5js and HTML/CSS for the event information and artist directory.

The 2024 MFA Thesis Exhibition featured 33 outstanding emerging artists and designers. Representing eight departments, these students’ ambitious and challenging research pushes beyond traditional disciplines to shape what is new and next in visual and material culture.

Big thanks to Shanice Aga, Ryan Sprowl, Chase Westfall and Lauren Thorson.

Lovetoread Italic

Typeface Design2024

Lovetoread Italic is reiterating Poligraphmash's Literaturnaya, a typeface created during the Soviet Union, through sub-cultural lens of "qiji" movement. This typeface cuts through Liteturnaya and creates space for online Azerbaijani emo culture to fit in. Special characters are made from symbols often used in Odnoklassniki and Facebook.

Collective Interface

Publication, Print, Website2024
Get your pamphlet here.

This pamphlet is weaving two texts, "Post-Internet City: Impressions of Disaster" by Nashin Mahtani and "Brand States: Postmodern Power, Democratic Pluralism, and Design" by Metahaven. The phone acts an interruptor but also an extension, referring to Nashin Mahtani's text, which employs people instead of the state during a disaster. The publication can be easily accessed by downloading the PDF on the website.

what i found under the tree

Installation, Website2023
Visit the project

"what i found under tree" (2023) reimagined themes of queer archive. The private corner facilitates an invitation to glance through someone's private computer and find diary entries from an unspecified individual about the trees and the sea. Specific contextual clues, from tree types in past neighborhoods to online collective representation of the Caspian sea carry themselves throughout the chapters of the pseudo-native experience. The experience doesn't reward the person with the secrets of the diary but instead expects an exchange of input, be it text, drawing or sound, in order to open up and share.

three windows: say hi.

Site Intervention, Installation, Website, Participatory2024

A webcam is a window. A screen is a window. A hole is a window. Using electronic objects as a mode of connection to the human body, “three aligned windows: say hi” explores the notions of digital intimacy, faux distance, permeated vision, and physical touch. Navigation of the body through the objects is transmitted through a confusing and laggy network of unreliable cables. Two rooms subvert the connection by not presenting what is wanted, keeping the curiosity unsatisfied but entertained.

webcameras, cables, screens, found glasses, vinyl.

Polyphonic Shimmering

Website, Publication2024
Visit the website here.

Polyphonic Shimmering is a collection of writing that shimmers and hums, playing with duration and pacing and expanding language beyond its conventional encasements. The 12 pieces that make up the publication allow us to see what their authors see, both visual and textual, but mostly through language that blurs the distinction between the two. The book and accompanying website were authored, designed, edited, and produced by the MFA students over the course of the semester from Meg Miller’s seminar.

Website designed and coded by me, khai tsng, Weitong Sun

Polyphonic Shimmering was featured in Kristoffer Tjalve’s Naive Weekly newsletter and Caitlin Dewey’s Links newsletter.

phoneSketches

Website, Mobile, Interactive2023-2024

Public and Private within JavaScript and forbidden taboo Facebook groups. These two p5js sketches explore public and private spaces with inverting the way it's being interacted with. One has the user put two fingers on the phone to show a private message shared in homoerotic Facebook groups, the other one functions as a scratch lottery to reveal love messages from a scam website gathered from a graffiti in Baku streets.

two cups and a secret

Performance, Participatory, Cups2024

A sonic sound travels through a thin nylon string to send a secret between two people. This uses simple cup telephone toy with a thinner connecting string to hide the relaying message and invite people to speak without showing the messenger.

Sound, Website, Participatory2024
Visit the website here.

A interactive publication where word sheets become guides for people to perform together at different speeds. Each language, each finger creates a personal tone and melody.

Unmute the videos to hear the harmony.

Loving or leaving a ship

Website, Digital2023
Visit the website

A fake website based on the 2012 Costa Concordia disaster. The website uses stock footage and basic HTML elements to tell a three act story of changed narrative. Done in Herdimas Anggara's Graduate Workshop "Algorithmic Trickery Deception, Metafiction, Subversion"
